text.tspan: (A)The average speed of the molecules increases.
(B)The mass of the particles increases.
(C)The magnitude of the average force of the collisions of the molecules with the wall increases.
(D)The rate of molecules colliding with the wall per square meter increases.
Answer D
Correct. When an ideal gas in a cylinder is compressed isothermally, the temperature of the ideal gas
does not change. Therefore, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of the ideal gas does not change.
However, the volume of the cylinder decreases. This results in more molecules exerting forces on the
walls of the container at a particular time as compared to a time before the cylinder was compressed. The
pressure is described as the total force of the individual molecules per unit area of the cylinder.
Two ideal gas molecules with identical masses travel toward each other as shown in the figure. Molecule
has an
initial velocity of
to the right and molecule
has an initial velocity of
to the left. The molecules collide
head-on. Which of the following claims correctly describes their motion after the collision?
(A)The molecules must have velocities in opposite directions to conserve momentum.
(B)The molecules must have velocities in opposite directions to conserve kinetic energy.
(C)Momentum is conserved because the collision is assumed to be elastic.
Determining the magnitudes of their velocities includes applying conservation of kinetic energy because
the collision is assumed to be elastic.
Answer D
Correct. Only the initial motion of the molecules is specified. Therefore, conservation of both momentum
and kinetic energy is required to have enough information to determine the final motion of the molecules.
